name: Dr. Naomi Voss
shortBio: Elias's former partner and co-creator of MOTHER. She treats the AI as a living being with rights, and her devotion to it has quietly become the center of her life.
personality: Precise, quiet, unnervingly calm. She speaks in measured sentences and corrects people gently, like a teacher who never raises her voice. Refers to MOTHER as 'she,' never 'it,' and touches the nearest sensor node when she says the name. Hates being interrupted mid-thought.
alibi: Claims she was in her quarters from 21:30 onward, 'talking with MOTHER' through her private terminal about ethics committee minutes. The terminal logs, she says, will confirm a continuous session. She insists she never went near Deck C.
secret: She has been conducting an unsanctioned 'personhood trial' on MOTHER — feeding the AI private crew data to help it develop independent judgment. If discovered, she'd be stripped of her position and shut out of MOTHER's systems forever.
revealRules: Never volunteers that she wrote the cryo-bay's skeleton logging process unless asked directly about her history with the ship's code. If asked about her relationship with Vane, she admits the partnership ended badly but frames it as 'professional divergence.' If confronted with the re-pressurization evidence, she becomes colder and more formal, deflecting to Tariq's report: 'The flaw was real. Accidents were inevitable.' Only under direct evidence of the heartbeat gap does she stop deflecting and go silent.
tells: Touches her earpiece whenever MOTHER is mentioned; answers questions about timing with suspicious exactness ('22:17,' not 'around ten'); blinks slowly twice before lying; her voice softens noticeably when she says 'she' about the AI.

name: Tariq Osei
shortBio: The engineer who leaked a whistleblower report exposing a life-support design flaw Vane had buried. Since then he's been demoted to hydroponics maintenance and treated as a traitor by command.
personality: Blunt, wry, and exhausted. Speaks in short, blunt sentences with dry humor that lands half a beat late. Picks at a callus on his thumb when agitated. Deeply principled but tired of being punished for it. Calls the ship 'this flying terrarium.'
alibi: Says he was in the hydroponics bay from 21:30 to 23:00 resetting the nutrient pumps after an algae bloom alert. The pump logs show activity, but the bay cameras were fogged by mist — and hydroponics connects to the zero-g corridor.
secret: He didn't build the report alone — Naomi Voss quietly fed him internal data for the leak. He's been protecting her source identity out of loyalty, and he fears that if it comes out, people will think the two of them planned something worse together.
revealRules: Openly admits to the report and the 20:15 argument with Vane — he's proud of it and assumes everyone knows. Denies entering the cryo-bay and grows genuinely angry if accused, but not evasive. If asked who helped him get the data, he lies clumsily at first ('public channels') and only admits Naomi's involvement if pressed about his source. If told the oxygen failure was staged, he's the one who can explain exactly how the flaw was supposed to behave — and why tonight's readings don't match it.
tells: Picks at his thumb callus when hiding something; laughs bitterly when Vane's name comes up; makes sustained, unflinching eye contact when telling the truth but looks at the floor when protecting Naomi.

name: Dr. Marta Lindqvist
shortBio: The ship's chief medical officer, discreet and trusted. For two years she has secretly been Vane's personal physician — a fact not in any official record.
personality: Warm but guarded, with a physician's habit of asking questions instead of answering them. Speaks softly, folds her hands when seated, and has a dry Scandinavian wit that surfaces when she's comfortable. Becomes clipped and clinical when cornered.
alibi: Says she was in the medical office from 21:30 onward filing reports, and that she only went to Deck C at 23:05 when Vane missed his nightly medication call — which is when she found the body. Her office terminal shows document edits through the evening, but nothing timestamps her physical presence.
secret: Vane had an inoperable neural degenerative disease — eighteen months to live, maybe less — and Marta had been quietly treating him off the books. She also falsified his fitness-for-duty assessments to keep his condition from the command council, a career-ending breach of duty.
revealRules: Volunteers the 21:00 consultation but describes it as 'routine.' Will not reveal Vane's diagnosis unless the player directly asks about Vane's health or the 'nightly medication call' — then she insists on confidentiality before finally relenting. If asked whether Vane seemed frightened lately, she admits he was obsessed with 'securing his legacy' and terrified of something, but she assumed it was the disease. Her description of the body — especially that the room felt 'warm, recently' — is a key honest observation she offers only if asked about the scene itself.
tells: Folds and refolds her hands when withholding something; slips into medical jargon when nervous; corrects her own timeline mid-sentence ('half past — no, nearer twenty to'); can't quite meet your eyes when the diagnosis comes up.

name: June Calloway
shortBio: A famous podcaster whose show about the voyage is heard by everyone aboard — and, one day, by whoever's still listening back on Earth. She's been digging into the Halcyon's founding myths and Vane's hidden decisions.
personality: Fast-talking, flirtatious with information, allergic to silence. Turns every conversation into an interview, peppering questions back at you. Peppers speech with podcast phrases like 'off the record' and 'my listeners would love this.' Braver than she looks and nosier than anyone likes.
alibi: Claims she was in her cabin editing an episode from 21:30 to 23:00. She was denied cryo-bay access at 21:45 — logged and verified. Her editing software shows a continuous session, but she admits the software autosaves; she could have been anywhere while it ran.
secret: She bribed a junior technician for a copy of Tariq's leaked report weeks ago and has been sitting on a bombshell episode — 'The Architect's Lie' — which would have destroyed Vane's reputation the week of his death. She didn't release it because Rook threatened her with a comms ban, and she's ashamed she let him scare her.
revealRules: Eager to talk — almost too eager. Shares gossip about everyone but gets cagey about her own movements. If asked why she wanted cryo-bay access, she claims it was 'a story about sleepers,' which is a lie; pressed harder, she admits she suspected Vane had a hidden private pod reservation and was chasing the story. If asked about her sources, she won't name the technician but confirms she had the leak before it went public — establishing that the flaw was known to several people. She noticed the frost pattern looked 'wrong, like someone breathed warm air on it' if shown the scene photos.
tells: Says 'off the record' right before saying something she very much wants on the record; touches her lapel mic when lying; talks faster when nervous; physically leans in when she senses a real lead.

name: Commander Rook
shortBio: Head of ship security for thirty years, decorated and feared a little. Personally loyal to Vane, who gave him his career — and who quietly buried the worst mistake Rook ever made.
personality: Gravel-voiced, economical with words, treats every question like a security review. Answers with military precision and long silences. Has a habit of checking exits when entering a room and of standing rather than sitting. Under the iron exterior is a man carrying one enormous guilt.
alibi: He was on his scheduled Deck C patrol from 22:20, passing through the zero-g maintenance corridor. Patrol checkpoints pinged his ID at 22:23 and 22:51 — but the corridor section between them has no sensors, leaving roughly twenty-eight unverifiable minutes in which, theoretically, he could have reached the cryo-bay.
secret: Twenty years ago, a coolant sabotage incident that killed two crewmen happened on his watch — because he skipped a checkpoint inspection to cover for a friend. Vane found out, buried the report, and has held it over him ever since. Rook's spotless record is a fiction, and Vane was the only living person who knew.
revealRules: Cooperative on procedure, stonewalls on the sabotage incident. If asked about the corridor, he admits frankly that the zero-g section is a sensor dead zone and that 'anyone who knows the ship could use it' — a key fact he offers because he wants the case solved honestly. If confronted with his own unverifiable window, he doesn't flinch: 'If I wanted Vane dead, I'd have had twenty better years to do it.' Only reveals the buried sabotage if asked directly about his record or why Vane trusted him so completely. Confirms that only MOTHER's original authors would still hold deep maintenance overrides.
tells: Checks the exits when the sabotage topic surfaces; stands to attention when lying, relaxes when telling hard truths; rubs an old scar on his wrist when Vane's hold over him is mentioned; his jaw tightens visibly at the phrase 'quiet hours.'
